questions.question: Explain how physical features affect where people live, with examples from South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: People settle on flat land, near water, on good farmland and on the coast. Mountains and dry areas have fewer people. So most South Africans live in the wetter east and the big cities of Gauteng and the coast, while the dry Karoo, Kalahari and Namaqualand have small towns far apart.

questions.question: Give three examples of how physical features affect the work people do.
questions.expected_answer: Fertile valleys with water, like the Hex River Valley, grow table grapes; the dry Karoo is used for sheep and goats; the flat Highveld with summer rain grows maize, and its minerals support gold and coal mining; and the coast supports harbours, fishing and tourism.

questions.question: Describe two ways people overcome physical features, and one cost of doing so.
questions.expected_answer: People build passes, tunnels and bridges through mountains, and dams, pipelines and canals to bring water, such as the tunnels from Lesotho to Gauteng; farmers use irrigation in dry areas. These are expensive, use a lot of energy and can harm the environment.
